newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Dostum, Masood forces meet on Afghanistan strategy.
newsitem.headline: Dostum, Masood forces meet on Afghanistan strategy.

text.p: Top commanders of former Afghan defence minister Ahmad Shah Masood and Uzbek warlord Abdul Rashid Dostum met on Tuesday to coordinate their strategy against the Taleban.

The commanders -- Abdul Bhir Salanghi for Masood and General Abdul Majid Ruzi for Dostum -- met on a blanket laid alongside the road outside Jabal os-Siraj, 90 km (60 miles) north of Taleban-occupied Kabul, under the watchful eyes of bodyguards.

Just a few hours earlier an unknown aircraft, presumably flying in support of the Taleban, had dropped two bombs, missing the town less than a kilometre (half a mile) away and hitting a nearby mountain.
Salanghi and Ruzi command troops along the seam between Masood's and Dostum's forces north of Kabul. Dostum has been estranged since 1994 from the Afghan government which he helped to bring to power.
He and Masood have fought fierce battles along the Salang highway which links Kabul with northern Afghanistan as recently as spring this year.
But the rise of the fundamentalist Islamic Taleban and their surprise capture of Kabul almost three weeks ago have thrown Masood and Dostum together in a way few thought possible.
No formal military alliance has been announced but it is clear that neither Masood, a Tajik, nor Dostum, an Uzbek, is prepared to submit to a Pashtun-dominated Taleban hegemony.
General Dostum on Monday acknowledged the legitimacy of president Burhannudin Rabbani whom the Taleban ousted from Kabul.

The Uzbek strongman is now bargaining from strength for his future role and responsibilities in a reconstituted government. His commanders have acknowledged providing some logistical support for Masood, but reporters have not found any evidence of joint military operations.

However, Tuesday's meeting between Salanghi and Ruzi and the sudden presence of some Dostum troops and heavy weapons, including tanks and truck-mounted anti-aircraft guns and rocket launchers around Jabal os-Siraj, suggested that may be about to change.
Prior to Tuesday, Dostum had held his men and equipment back at the top of the Salang Pass, about an hour's drive north of Jabal os-Siraj.

"I think Dostum and Masood are moving towards a joint offensive to retake Kabul but they are willing to take their time and get it right," said an aid worker in northern Afghanistan who is familiar with both of the commanders.
"Certainly all the talk among their men is that they are going to Kabul. It may take a while to get things organised."

As a Masood-Dostum alliance appeared to be taking shape, government troops reportedly retook the market town of Qara Bagh about 50 km (30 miles) north of Kabul. The town has changed hands at least three times in the last week.
Masood forces reported continued progress around Bagram military airfield, also north of Kabul and near Sarobi, which is 70 km (45 miles) east of the capital.
